title: They feared people more than they feared Allah.
subtitle: When the wrong fear runs your life
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the hypocrites {trap}feared the believers more than they feared Allah{/trap}, citing another verse about people who fear men as they fear Allah or more. He calls this {reward}good news for the believers{/reward}. The cause: {idea}they are a people who do not understand.{/idea}
now: You would never skip prayer in front of your father. But alone in the hotel room, it is easy. You would never lie to your boss's face. But to Allah, quietly, you do. {idea}Notice whose eyes you actually feel on you.{/idea}
old: I behave well when people are watching. That is what matters.
new: The eyes that matter most are Allah's, and they are always on me.
try: Do one act today you only ever do in front of others, but this time alone.

title: They look united, but their hearts are divided.
subtitle: Togetherness on the outside, rivalry inside
then: Ibn Kathir explains they would only face the believers {trap}from behind fortified walls, out of fear.{/trap} Among themselves, the hostility was intense. {idea}You would think they were united, but their hearts are divided{/idea}, because they did not reason.
now: The family that smiles together in the Eid photo and does not speak once the camera is down. The team that shares the same logo and talks behind each other's backs. {idea}Real unity is in the hearts, not the group shot.{/idea}
old: As long as we look united, we are united.
new: Unity lives in hearts that want the same good, not in appearances.
try: Settle one quiet grudge with someone in your family or team today.

title: The same story had just happened, close by.
subtitle: A recent lesson they did not learn

row.title: it will not happen to me

then: Ibn Kathir says, according to Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Ibn Ishaq, the people {idea}shortly before them{/idea} were the tribe of Bani Qaynuqa, who had already {trap}tasted the bad result of their conduct.{/trap} The lesson was recent and close, and still unheeded.
now: Your colleague got fired for cutting corners. Your cousin's marriage broke over hidden debts. You watched it happen, close up. {idea}The verse asks: did you learn, or are you walking the same road?{/idea}
old: Other people's mistakes have nothing to do with me.
new: When I see where a path led someone close to me, that is my warning too.
try: Think of one mistake you watched someone make. Check you are not doing a smaller version.

title: Shaytan says: do it. Then: I have nothing to do with you.
subtitle: The friend who disappears after the fall
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites' broken promises to Bani an-Nadir were {trap}just like Shaytan{/trap}: he lures a person into disbelief, and once they obey, {trap}he disowns them{/trap} and declares himself free of their actions, saying he fears Allah.
now: The friend who said, just one drink, everyone does it, and then was nowhere when it went wrong. The voice in your head that says, go on, no one will know, and then leaves you alone with the guilt. {idea}Same pattern. Different costume.{/idea}
old: The ones pushing me to do wrong will be there with me afterwards.
new: Whoever pushes me toward wrong will abandon me once I fall.
try: Next time you hear go on, do it, pause and ask: who will stand with me after?

title: The tempter and the tempted end up in the same place.
subtitle: Disowning each other does not change the outcome
then: The parable ends soberly. Ibn Kathir says the end of both, {trap}Shaytan who commanded disbelief, and those who accepted his call{/trap}, is the same. {idea}This is the recompense of every unjust person.{/idea}
now: I only did it because they pressured me. The excuse feels solid. But the verse puts both people side by side. {idea}Pressure explains a choice. It does not erase it.{/idea} The good news: you can still choose differently today.
old: If someone else pushed me, the blame is mostly theirs.
new: I am responsible for what I choose, whoever pushed me toward it.
try: Own one choice today that you have been blaming on someone else.

title: Look at what you have sent ahead for tomorrow.
subtitle: The verse that filled two heaps of charity
then: Poor people from Mudar came to the Prophet ﷺ, and his face changed at their state. He recited this verse and urged giving, {reward}even half a date.{/reward} An Ansari brought a bag he could barely lift, others followed, and {reward}his face shone like gold.{/reward} Ibn Kathir: {idea}hold yourselves accountable before you are judged.{/idea}
now: Your bank app shows what you saved for next year. Your calendar shows what you planned for next month. {idea}What does your account for tomorrow, the real one, show?{/idea} Even half a date counts. And one person starting can move a whole room.
old: Tomorrow means next week's plans and next year's savings.
new: Tomorrow is the Day I meet Allah, and I am sending things there now.
try: Tonight, spend two minutes reviewing your day, and send one good deed ahead before sleep.

title: Forget Allah, and you end up forgetting yourself.
subtitle: What you lose when remembrance goes
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do not forget the remembrance of Allah, or He will make you forget the good deeds that would benefit you{/trap}, since recompense matches the action. He links it to another verse: {idea}let not your wealth or children divert you from His remembrance.{/idea}
now: Busy season at work. You stop reading Quran, then morning dhikr, then you are rushing prayers. A month later you barely recognise yourself: short-tempered, empty, scrolling at 2 a.m. {idea}Losing Allah is how you lose you.{/idea}
old: I am too busy for remembrance right now. I will come back to it.
new: When I let go of remembering Allah, I start losing myself too.
try: Set one fixed daily moment for dhikr, even one minute, and start it today.

title: The two outcomes are not equal.
subtitle: Paradise and the Fire are not the same ending

key.label: Does it matter how I live

then: Ibn Kathir explains these two groups are {idea}never the same in Allah's judgement{/idea}, citing verses that ask if those who do evil think they will be treated like those who believe and do good. {reward}Allah will honour the righteous.{/reward}
now: Some days it feels like it does not matter: the honest and the cheat both get the promotion, both buy the same car. {idea}The verse says the endings are not equal.{/idea} What you choose matters more than how the middle looks.
old: In the end, good and bad people all end up the same.
new: The ending is not the same. How I live decides which group I join.
try: Make one choice today because of where it leads, not how it looks now.

title: A mountain would crumble under this Quran. What about your heart?
subtitle: The weight of revelation

picture.label: If it came down on a mountain

then: Ibn Kathir asks: if a huge, hard mountain that understood the Quran would crumble from fear of Allah, {idea}why do your hearts not soften?{/idea} He recalls the tree trunk that {reward}wept like a child{/reward} when the Prophet ﷺ moved to a new minbar. Al-Hasan said: you are more worthy to miss him than the trunk.
now: You play recitation in the background while cooking, while driving, while answering emails. It is just sound. {idea}Words that would split a mountain, and you are half-listening.{/idea}
old: The Quran is something I listen to in the background.
new: These words could split a mountain. They deserve my full heart.
try: Listen to one page of Quran today doing nothing else, and let it reach you.

title: He knows the hidden and the seen, and He is merciful.
subtitle: Knowledge and mercy, side by side
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}knows all that we see and all we cannot, even ants in the darkness.{/idea} Then in the same verse: He is Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim, {reward}owner of a mercy that embraces all creation{/reward}, in this life and the next.
now: Someone who knew every secret of yours would be terrifying. Unless they were also the kindest being in existence. {reward}That is exactly who this verse describes.{/reward} Fully known, and still met with mercy.
old: Being completely known by Allah is something to fear.
new: The One who knows everything about me is also the Most Merciful.
try: Tell Allah one thing you are ashamed of, then ask for His mercy by name: Ya Rahman.

title: The King, the Pure, Peace, the Giver of safety.
subtitle: Eight names in one verse
then: Ibn Kathir explains each name. As-Salam: {idea}free from any defect.{/idea} Al-Mu'min: He gives His servants safety by promising He will never wrong them. He cites the hadith qudsi: {trap}might is My lower garment and pride My cloak; whoever disputes Me in either, I will punish.{/trap}
now: You feel unsafe, maybe in a new city, a new job, or a hard diagnosis. {idea}One of His names is Al-Mu'min, the One who gives safety and never wrongs you.{/idea} And when your ego swells after a win, remember who alone owns greatness.
old: I have to be the one in control and the one who looks great.
new: He is the King, the Giver of safety, and greatness belongs only to Him.
try: Pick one name from this verse and call on Allah by it in your next dua.

title: He measured you, brought you out, and shaped you.
subtitle: The Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner
then: The surah closes as it opened, with everything glorifying Him. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}Al-Khaliq measures and proportions; Al-Bari brings into being what He measured{/idea}; Al-Musawwir gives it its form. None but Allah can do all three. {reward}To Him belong the best names.{/reward}
now: You look in the mirror and list everything you would change. The verse says your measure, your existence and your form {idea}were each chosen by the Fashioner.{/idea} Whatever you work on, start from that.
old: I am just the sum of my flaws.
new: I was measured, brought into being, and shaped by the One with the best names.
try: Look in a mirror today and say: Ya Musawwir, thank You for shaping me.
